clue.text: A weird memento given by the king shows how the wind blows!

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing that shows how the wind is blowing

indicators.note: weird means strange or odd, so the letters of the word memento are scrambled

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands in crosswords for the monarch; here loosely 'the king'

explanation.surface: Someone is handed a strange keepsake by the king, and it reveals which way the wind blows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' makes NEMOMET; the definition is descriptive, 'something that shows how the wind blows', and the exclamation mark nods to the surface's weather-vane feel.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures wind speed, so it literally tells you how hard the breeze is blowing.

clue.text: Not oneself, certainly not — gone berserk!

parts.note: a firm refusal: no

indicators.note: going berserk means running wild, so the letters of gone are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is not themselves at all, having gone completely berserk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'berserk' gives NEGO. The answer is a philosophers' term, rarely met outside crosswords, for all that is not the self.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy, everything outside the self, the external world, is termed the not-self.

clue.text: Foreign nobleman proceeds east

parts.note: to proceed steadily is to march; 'proceeds' gives marches
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An overseas aristocrat sets off eastward.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian marquis carries this title, a rank of nobility abroad.

clue.text: Exotic fruit is sent — no game ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so sent, no and game are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some unusual fruit has been dispatched, though no game was requested.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and 'is' are links; 'ordered' looks like 'requested' but signals the anagram of SENT NO GAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical purple-skinned fruit from South-East Asia, prized for its sweet white segments.

clue.text: Giving trusted leader cause for treachery

indicators.note: a word's leader is its opening letter, here the start of trusted

parts.note: a cause is a reason for something

explanation.surface: Someone gives a trusted chief good grounds to suspect betrayal.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or sovereign is the gravest form of disloyalty.

clue.text: Stern nurse

definitions.meaning: the stern is the back end of a ship
to nurse a child is to bring it up

explanation.definitionFit: The back of a vessel is its hindmost part, and bringing up young is raising them.

clue.text: This determines how much a person has up top!

definitions.text: This determines how much a person has up top!

parts.words: This determines how much a person has up top!
parts.note: 'up top' suggests brains, but it means on the head: the boundary where growth on the scalp begins shows how much is there

explanation.definitionFit: The edge of growth on the forehead marks how far a person's thatch extends.

clue.text: Used in 27 for increasing strain

parts.note: 'strain' suggests stress, but it is a plant variety: a heated box used in a glasshouse to raise more plants

explanation.walkthrough: 27 is the glasshouse answer; 'increasing strain' means multiplying a plant variety, not adding pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated seed tray in which gardeners raise cuttings and seedlings to multiply plants.

clue.text: City retreat where French pastry is served

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
a lair is an animal's hiding place or den

explanation.surface: A hideaway in town where continental cakes are offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is served' is a link; the City is the City of London, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: A long choux bun filled with cream and topped with chocolate icing.

clue.text: Delight in appearance on stage

definitions.meaning: to delight is to enchant or put under a spell
an actor's coming on to the stage

explanation.definitionFit: Enchanting someone is putting them in a trance; an actor's arrival in a scene is the other sense, stressed differently.

clue.text: In-flight cabaret for travellers waiting for the take-off?

definitions.text: In-flight cabaret for travellers waiting for the take-off?

parts.words: In-flight cabaret for travellers waiting for the take-off?
parts.note: read as a striptease in the sky, a show where the audience awaits the 'take-off' of clothes; really a runway where planes take off

explanation.definitionFit: A simple landing strip for light aircraft, where passengers wait for their plane to depart.

clue.text: Figure on entering the Church

indicators.note: entering means going into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A notable person joining the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric solid tapering from a round base to a point is a shape in geometry.

clue.text: Feature article about nippy little furry animal

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
nippy weather is chilly; chill means coldness
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A magazine piece about a cold, small, fluffy creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a loose link meaning 'concerning'; the A comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A small South American rodent bred for its very soft grey fur.

clue.text: The time for growth's about over, so putting up the money

indicators.note: about means around, so the time of year encloses the other pieces

parts.note: spring is the season when plants grow
on can mean over, as in resting on top of
taken as written

explanation.surface: The growing season is nearly finished, so someone is funding things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; 'over' as ON (resting on top) is a common crossword equivalence that newcomers often miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing an event or person financially is funding them as a patron.

clue.text: Still state guns may be turned on people

indicators.note: turned round means read backwards, applied to the word for guns

parts.note: gats are slang for guns
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: In a frozen situation, weapons might be aimed at a population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be turned' gives STAG from gangster slang for guns; in a down clue 'on' means placed above the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A condition with no movement or growth, like a stagnant pond or economy.

clue.text: The whole thing is green — it's revolting

indicators.note: revolting means rising up or overturning, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: it, with the 's as is, a link

explanation.surface: Everything is green, and it is disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolting' looks like 'disgusting' but signals the anagram of GREEN IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A whole number, with no fraction, is a complete unit in arithmetic.

clue.text: A temporary housing hold-up

parts.note: 'hold-up' suggests a delay or robbery, but it is a support holding up a canvas shelter

explanation.definitionFit: A canvas shelter is temporary housing, and the upright stake supports it.

clue.text: Split with some purpose in dress

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a rent is a tear or split
an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: Tear something deliberately in a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: An old literary word for clothing or garments.

clue.text: The musician's fading away as the fellow is able to act

parts.note: a man is a fellow
can means is able
to do is to act

explanation.surface: A performer is dying out while a man is still able to perform.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian musical direction meaning dying away, used by performers for diminishing volume.

clue.text: Shake and strive to restrain an unruly youngster

indicators.note: restraining means holding in, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or strive
a brat is a badly behaved child

explanation.surface: Someone trembles while struggling to control a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: To quiver rapidly back and forth is to tremble.

clue.text: Protocol for the meeting

definitions.meaning: accepted custom or rules of behaviour
a large formal gathering or conference

explanation.definitionFit: An accepted custom is one sense, and a conference of members is the other.

clue.text: Almost left

definitions.meaning: on a horse or vehicle, the left side is called this side

explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means close; with horses and British cars the left-hand side is the nearside.

clue.text: Moderates put a graduate up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, reversing everything before it

parts.note: to set something is to put it
BA is a Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: Restrained types promote a university leaver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SET A BA, giving ABATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessens or eases, as a storm or pain dies down.

clue.text: The foreign dealer who's mean with little hesitation

parts.note: to import can mean to signify or mean
er is a short hesitating sound

explanation.surface: An overseas trader is described as stingy and slightly hesitant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' looks like 'stingy' but is the verb: to import is to signify.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant who brings goods in from abroad trades in overseas products.

clue.text: Some of the most angelic children may need a smack

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Even the best-behaved children sometimes need a slap.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'children may need a smack' as the definition, but only 'smack' (a flavour) means the answer; the rest is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A smack is a distinct taste or flavour, a sharp savour.

clue.text: Made a meal of outside right wanting a transfer

annotationWithheld.why: Made a meal of outside right wanting a transfer: ALIEN (outside) + ATE (made a meal of) leaves 'right wanting a transfer' with no clear role; no parse uses every word once
annotationWithheld.clue: Made a meal of outside right wanting a transfer

clue.text: The woman's taken ill — in a bad way

indicators.note: in a bad way means disordered, so the letters ill and in a are rearranged

explanation.surface: She has been taken sick and is in a poor state.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s taken' is a link; 'in a' is fodder and 'bad way' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it stands for any female person.

clue.text: Home where there's real concern for the environment?

definitions.text: Home where there's real concern for the environment?

parts.words: Home where there's real concern for the environment?
parts.note: read as an eco-friendly household; really a glass structure where plants are given a controlled climate

explanation.definitionFit: A glass building for growing plants, where the surroundings are carefully controlled.
